newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Newcastle Australia exports big grain volume.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Newcastle Australia exports big grain volume.

text.p: The Newcastle grain terminal in the Australian state of New South Wales (NSW) would this month export more than 220,000 tonnes of wheat, the largest tonnage shipped through the terminal in one month in the past decade, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in a statement.
Guidelines drawn up for the 1996 export programme called for exports of about 120,000 tonnes a month from Newcastle, it said.

The export amount would be almost doubled this month through planning by AWB's logistics division, even distribution of shipping and work by storage and handling group GrainCorp and Freight Rail to assemble the tonnage, it said.
The AWB was this year predicting national wheat production of about 19 million tonnes, with NSW contributing significantly to that, it said.
The NSW season had progressed exceptionally so far throughout most of the grainbelt, John Arrigo, AWB NSW logistics manager said.
"We are expecting the largest crop in a decade," he said.
"We expect to see a very well managed harvest come November," he said.
It was planned this year to repeat last season's strategy of maximising returns to NSW growers by front-ending the shipping programme, he said.
The current forecast for exports in 1996/97 from Newcastle terminal was between 1.5 and 2.0 million tonnes, with total exports from NSW significantly higher than in previous years, he said.
